system.name: ReCycle
system.one_liner: a system for resilient DNN training that reroutes microbatches to data-parallel peers and adapts the pipeline schedule to tolerate worker failures without spare servers

content.subject: how ReCycle's worker grid tolerates worst-case single-group failures versus scattered 8-worker failures across a pipeline

content.key_idea: ReCycle keeps training alive as long as at least one worker per pipeline stage survives across the data-parallel peers, even losing an entire data-parallel group at one stage (a) or 8 of 12 workers scattered across the grid (b).
content.reading_order: each panel's grid read left to right along a row (one data-parallel pipeline's stages), top to bottom across the three rows; panel (a) first highlights the dashed 'Data Parallel Group lost' column, panel (b) shows the same grid with a more scattered failure pattern

encoding.emphasis: the dashed red 'Data Parallel Group lost' box in panel (a) calls out the one named worst-case pattern the text discusses, while panel (b) relies on the sheer count of red X icons (8 of 12) to make its point
reusable_patterns: an identical worker grid (data-parallel rows x pipeline-parallel columns) redrawn once per failure scenario, with only the active/failed colour pattern changing between panels
a dashed callout box isolating one failed group of cells that share a column

summary: Figure 7 compares two concrete failure scenarios to illustrate ReCycle's fault-tolerance guarantees on a 3-way-data-parallel by 4-way-pipeline-parallel worker grid (12 workers, labelled W_x_y). In (a), the worst case for a single data-parallel group, all three workers at pipeline stage 1 fail together (dashed red box, 'Data Parallel Group lost'), yet each row still reroutes around its own missing stage-1 worker and continues. In (b), 8 of the 12 workers fail, two-thirds of the GPUs, scattered so that every pipeline stage still keeps exactly one active worker (W1_0, W0_1, W2_2, W1_3). Green GPU icons and green labels mark active workers, red GPU-with-X icons and red labels mark failed ones, and red arrows mark stage-to-stage hops that the text ties to ReCycle's microbatch rerouting. Both panels support the same underlying rule: training continues as long as one live worker remains per pipeline stage.
